item.title: Certifying Reward Alignment in Portfolio Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.34153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial reinforcement learning often translates an investment objective into an additive risk-adjusted reward. An agent can optimise that reward accurately yet implement a different financial preference. We develop a decision audit for terminal mean-variance equilibrium that separates reward misspecification from learning error. In a finite exogenous-state market, we bound the gain from changing one action using actor, reward and continuation-critic residuals. The certificate ignores state-constant critic offsets, accommodates convex action constraints, and has an independent-sample extension that does not require the equilibrium policy. A continuation-aware actor-critic method estimates the future-policy correction from samples. Across nine controlled markets and twenty seeds, it reduces policy distance by and one-step deviation gain by relative to a matched myopic-reward network. A separate PPO comparison tests the same reward intervention within a standard optimiser. Historical tests cross seven covariance estimators and 10, 30 and 49 US industry portfolios over 432 months: joint reward calibration preserves each fitted mean-variance target, but does not improve realised investment performance. Together, these results provide a way to quantify whether a learned decision implements its stated financial objective, separately from how well that objective performs in a backtest.
item.dc:creator: Matin Tavakoli, Seyedreza Tavakoli, Faezeh Salmani, Amir Amini, Mohammad Hosein Rohban, Gholamali Aminian, Ali Habibnia Rohban

item.title: Optimal portfolio choice under green transition timing risk
item.description: arXiv:2610.33597v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study an investor's optimal portfolio choice problem when they account for the impact of a possible future green transition, whose timing is uncertain. We model the green transition as a discontinuity in the stock price processes, driven by a single jump process with constant intensity, in which 'green' stocks increase in value and 'brown' stocks decrease in value. The investor is ambiguous about the timing of the green transition and designs an investment strategy which is robust to this risk. The investor has constant relative risk aversion preferences over both wealth and model ambiguity, which introduce a multiplicative ambiguity penalty for power utility and an additive ambiguity penalty for log utility. We separate the problem into pre- and post-transition cases, derive the solution, and provide a verification theorem. We further show that the log utility, ambiguity-neutral, and worst-case problems are obtained as special cases of our general problem. In a case study with one green and one brown stock, we show that when the stock prices are positively correlated, an investor who is aware of transition risk increases their investment in the green stock and reduces their investment in the brown stock, compared to when they ignore the possibility of a transition. We illustrate the difference between an ambiguity-averse and a risk-averse investor, and show how an ambiguity-averse investor re-allocates their portfolio as their view on the probability of a green transition changes.
item.dc:creator: Emma Kroell, Mogens Steffensen

item.title: Bayesian Parametric Portfolio Policies
item.description: arXiv:2602.21173v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametric portfolio policies map predictors into portfolio weights without modelling returns, making them a natural tool for factor timing. With many predictors, if the policy has more coefficients than observations the data cannot pin it down. We develop Bayesian Parametric Portfolio Policies (BPPP), which discipline the policy with a prior, update it with realised utility, and average the weights over the posterior. We contribute to the factor-timing literature by estimating timing as a portfolio rule rather than from return forecasts. With 242 predictors and five factors, BPPP earns 2.08 percentage points a year from timing, mostly from aggregate anomaly returns. Under a leverage limit, averaging sizes each position by its uncertainty and comes close, without a separate scale choice, to the size that maximises timing with hindsight. A turnover penalty preserves significant gross timing at lower turnover.
item.dc:creator: Miguel C. Herculano

item.title: Market Regime-Based Multi-Asset Portfolio Optimization Using Nested Clustered Optimization for Tactical Asset Allocation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a regime-aware tactical asset allocation (TAA) framework integrating Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) regime detection with Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) for multi-asset portfolio construction. Market regimes (Bullish, Sideways, Bearish) are identified strictly out of sample to prevent look-ahead bias, parameterizing regime-conditional covariance estimation and hierarchical clustering within NCO. The framework is evaluated on a monthly Indonesian multi-asset universe comprising government bonds (SBN), LQ45 equities, gold, CNY/IDR foreign exchange, and Bitcoin over a 56-month out-of-sample period (2021-2025). Benchmarks include equal-weight (1/N), buy-and-hold, minimum variance, hierarchical risk parity (HRP), and standard regime-agnostic NCO. Statistical significance is evaluated using the Jobson-Korkie test. The empirical results demonstrate that Regime-NCO effectively curbs tail risk, achieving a maximum drawdown of 4.44% compared with 15.27% for equal-weight and 21.17% for buy-and-hold. However, regime-agnostic NCO achieves a still lower drawdown of 2.19% and higher cumulative return (29.57% vs 5.44%). Detailed analysis reveals that a rolling 24-month HMM triggers regime transitions in 55 of 56 out-of-sample months, inducing regime drift that erodes the theoretical gains of conditional covariance estimation. These findings provide candid empirical evidence on rolling HMM behavior and highlight the necessity of transition-smoothing mechanisms for practical regime-aware portfolio optimization.
